title: Memory Waterfall Allocator: proactive headspace & waterfall budgeting for weights/KV/activations
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Problem: OOMs and high tail latencies during mixed interactive and batch workloads are traced to static headroom allocations and brittle KV/activation partitioning. Current slab/static quotas either over-reserve (raising cost) or under-provision (causing OOMs and degraded P99.9 latency).

Goal: Design and implement a Memory Waterfall Allocator (MWA) that: (1) maintains a small, dynamically adjustable proactive headspace to absorb microbursts; (2) budgets memory across three domains (weights, KV cache, activations) using a waterfall policy where lower-priority domains yield to higher-priority realtime work; (3) integrates short-term forecasting to size headspace per tenant/route; and (4) exposes runtime telemetry and a safe rollout plan with canary checks.

Acceptance criteria:
- MWA reduces OOMs by >= 85% on mixed workloads in staging (relative to baseline).
- P99.9 token latency regression <= 10% for critical routes; overall median latency unchanged or improved.
- Cost per token (runtime GPU time) change within +/-5% for normal traffic profiles.
- Metrics and dashboards (token-level, kv-hit-ratio, eviction-rate, headspace-utilization) available in console.
- Rollout plan with automatic fallback to current allocator on safety thresholds (OOM spike or error-rate spike).

High-level design:
1) Waterfall tiers and priorities:
   - Weights: pinned resident memory — hard-reserved region and quantization-aware sizing.
   - Headspace reserve: small elastic buffer that is recharged via short-term forecast (lookahead 3-10s) and reclaimed after bursts.
   - Activations: transient working set; uses eviction/coalesce strategies when needed.
   - KV cache: best-effort cache with tiered eviction (LRU-ish with cost-awareness) and optional compress-on-evict pipelines.

2) Allocation model:
   - Soft quotas per domain computed from model profile (weights size, typical KV footprint per recent sessions, activation per-token growth) plus forecasted burst margin.
   - Waterfall policy enforcement: when demand exceeds total usable memory, evict/trim from lowest priority domain (KV first, then activations) until headroom satisfies in-flight requests.
   - Hysteresis windows and grace periods to avoid oscillation (exponential backoff on reclaims).

3) Forecasting and proactive headspace sizing:
   - Lightweight on-node predictor using EWMA of recent token arrival rates + short adaptive multiplier based on route/tenant profile.
   - Forecast feeds periodic headspace top-ups; cap top-ups by measured spare capacity and safety multiplier.

4) Compatibility and fail-safes:
   - Hard-cap safety fallback: if any eviction fails to recover enough memory within X ms, fast-fail request and record incident.
   - Rollback hook: quick switch to legacy allocator (safe, stable) via config flag per pool.

Implementation plan:
- Phase A (prototype, 1 sprint): in-memory simulator + microbench harness that replays token arrival traces and KV access patterns.
- Phase B (local canary, 2 sprints): implement MWA in runtime with a feature flag, deploy to a small group of dedicated GPUs, collect telemetry.
- Phase C (wide canary & safety gates, 2 sprints): progressively increase traffic, integrate console dashboards and automatic rollback triggers.

Telemetry & experiments:
- New metrics: headspace_allocated, headspace_used, kv_evictions/sec, kv_compress_ratio, activation_trim_events, ooms_by_domain, allocator_decisions{route,tenant}.
- Benchmarks: replay three historical traces: steady background, interactive bursty, mixed PLG + enterprise spikes.
- Experiments: compare compressed-KV on-evict vs instant-evict (CPU compress latency trade-off), and headspace size multiplier sensitivity sweep.

Trade-offs & open questions:
- Aggressive KV compression reduces memory pressure but increases CPU latency and may hurt throughput; need per-model/per-pool knobs.
- Forecast accuracy vs cost: heavier predictors give better headspace sizing but cost CPU; choose lightweight predictors first.
- Multi-tenant fairness: waterfall could starve noisy neighbors; consider per-tenant minimum guarantees and eviction decay curves.

Safety checklist:
- Automated canary abort on >3x baseline OOM rate, >2x error rate, or P99.9 latency spike >20% for critical routes.
- Audit logs for every allocation decision and eviction action for postmortem.
- Feature flag and runtime config to set per-pool policies.

Next steps & deliverables:
- Build and open the simulator repo (link below).
- RFC: detailed allocator algorithm and knobs (deliverable to P0 stakeholders).
- Prototype PR with basic waterfall and headspace top-up loop.
